title: Zero the first line on the CR refusal path and pty-prove it (WCLI-134 opus follow-up)
description: Follow-up from the opus APPROVE at 634a1b3 of ward-cli#253 (WCLI-134), items 3/B (LOW), A (LOW), D and E (NIT). On the CR refusal path, consumeLineFeedAfterReturn throws in secret-value.ts before value exists, so the first line of the refused paste stays in the bytes number[] and the next byte in next until GC; the value.fill(0) after the read never runs. Wrapping the loop in readHiddenValueBytes in try/catch, zeroing bytes and next, then rethrowing also covers the too_large residue and the never-zeroed number[] source behind new Uint8Array(bytes). Every pty scenario uses newline terminators, so the CR path has no real-tty proof. Nits D (hard-coded 30 and 0x1 instead of QUIET_MS and POLLIN) and E (an empty value then CR and a byte refuses as multiline while the comment promises the empty-read terms) are optional.

acceptanceCriteria.text: When a CR-terminated paste is refused inside readHiddenValueBytes, the bytes read so far and the byte read after the CR are zeroed before the error propagates, and a test fails if that zeroing is dropped
The too_large path also zeroes the bytes it read before refusing
A pty scenario pastes s3cret then CR LEAK-ONE CR LEAK-TWO CR and observes the multiline refusal with nothing reaching the shell
A pty accepting control pastes s3cret then CR LF and observes LEN:6

implementationNotes: Built on fix/wcli-136-cr-refusal-zeroing. readHiddenValueBytes now zeroes bytes, its one-byte buffer and the byte read after a CR in a finally, so the CR refusal, the too_large refusal, an abandoned read and a returning read all clear them; consumeLineFeedAfterReturn takes the caller-owned next buffer. A HiddenReadScratch handle lets a test see all three after every exit. Nit D done: QUIET_MS and POLLIN are exported from terminal-input.ts and used in the CR consume. Nit E left (fails closed, optional). Evidence: test secret.test.ts "a refused read zeroes what it read, and so does a read that returns" (turns red with the bytes zeroing or the next zeroing removed, each run); pty-residue.test.ts gains the CR multiline refusal (REFUSED:secret_value_multiline, nothing reaches the shell) and the CRLF accepting control (LEN:6), both passing on darwin, and the accepting control turns red when the LF after a CR is no longer consumed. bun run check passes (1173), lore check clean. The CI runner skips pty cases, so the pty proof is a local darwin run.

OPUS REVIEW VERDICT, recorded verbatim (reviewer: leader-spawned DEC-183 Stage 1 reviewer unit ward-cli-review-256, model claude-opus-5-5; header below; received by team-lead 2026-11-03 ~14:58Z):

Reviewer: leader-spawned DEC-183 Stage 1 reviewer unit ward-cli-review-256, model claude-opus-5-5 (spawn-model verify MATCH, pid 57978), read-only, no shell. Received by team-lead 2026-11-03 ~14:58Z. Findings come from reading only.

I found nothing HIGH or MEDIUM. Items 3/B, A and D from the #253 verdict are fixed. Nit E is left, as the writer disclosed, and it fails closed.

ANSWERS TO THE BRIEF'S QUESTIONS
1. The returned value is not zeroed. `return new Uint8Array(bytes)` (src/adapters/secret-value.ts:159) is evaluated before the `finally` (:160-164) runs, and `new Uint8Array(number[])` makes an independent copy, so `bytes.fill(0)` touches only the source. Ctrl-C returns a fresh `new Uint8Array(0)` (:149). The `number[]` source is now zeroed on every path, including the success path, which also closes the pre-existing residue from item 3. A regression is pinned: the test's `run("token\r\n", "token")` decodes the returned array after the `finally` has run, so a zeroed return would read as NULs and go red.
2. Every exit reaches the `finally`. These are all inside the `try` (:139-159):
   - `readOnce` rethrowing a non-EAGAIN/EINTR error (:87), whether it reads the main buffer or `next`
   - a throw from `pollInput` in the CR consume (:102)
   - the multiline throw (:106) and too_large (:156)
   - the Ctrl-C return and the normal return
   Before the `try` there are only two 1-byte allocations and three property writes (:133-138), none of which can throw on input.
3. HiddenReadScratch does not keep secrets alive any longer. Production calls `readHiddenValueBytes(0)` (:197) with the default `{}`, which dies with the call. The handle only ever points at arrays the `finally` has zeroed. It is a test seam in an exported signature (an optional second parameter). `withInput` calls `run(descriptor)` with one argument, so the existing `withInput(..., readHiddenValueBytes)` call sites cannot pass a stray scratch. NIT at most.
4. Revert analysis, by reading. A poll on a regular-file fd reports POLLIN, so `next` really is exercised over `withInput`.
   - Drop `bytes.fill`: red on all four cases.
   - Drop `buffer.fill`: red. The buffer is left holding 0x0d for the refusal, 'a' for too_large, 0x0a for the token case, or 0x03 for the abandoned read.
   - Drop `next.fill`: red. `next` is left holding 'L' for the refusal or 0x0a for token\r\n.
   - Revert the whole try/finally: red.
5. I found no new defect in the CR/LF consume. It is unchanged apart from taking the caller's `next`. The shared constants are the same values (30, 0x1) and are only newly exported (terminal-input.ts:47, :55).

FINDINGS
- LOW (test gap). In test/secret.test.ts, "a refused read zeroes what it read, and so does a read that returns", the check `scratch.bytes?.every(b => b === 0)` is vacuously true on an empty array. Only the refusal and too_large cases pin `bytes.length`. So if `bytes.fill(0)` were changed to `bytes.length = 0`, the token and abandoned (ab^C) cases would still pass. The two pinned cases would still catch it, so this does not block. A fix would be to assert the expected length on all four cases.
- NIT (pty discrimination). The CR refusal scenario (pty-residue.test.ts, "a carriage-return multiline paste is refused...") would stay green even with `consumeLineFeedAfterReturn` removed, because the queue probe would refuse the queued "LEAK-ONE" anyway. It proves what AC2 asks for (the refusal, and nothing reaching the shell), but not that the CR path is the one refusing. The CRLF accepting control is the real discriminator. LEN:6 is reachable only if `\r` arrives unmapped and the LF is consumed. If ICRNL were set, the input would arrive as `s3cret\n\n` and be refused. So the writer's green darwin run, together with the writer's mutation (accepting control red when the LF is not consumed), also closes the #253 verdict's unverified ICRNL inference, at least for Bun's setRawMode. That is the same raw-mode call production makes (defaultSetRaw, secret-value.ts:54-58).
- NIT (comment overclaims). The doc comment at secret-value.ts:125-128 says the bytes read so far are zeroed. `fill(0)` zeroes only the indices the array currently holds. A byte removed by backspace `bytes.pop()` (:152) is never overwritten, and the old backing stores left behind as `push` grows the array are not reachable. Whether JSC clears either one cannot be determined by reading. This is best-effort hygiene in a GC'd runtime. A one-word softening ("the bytes still held") would make it exact.
- LOW, OUT OF SCOPE and pre-existing (a suggested follow-up task, not a reason to hold #256). `readPassphraseBytes` (src/adapters/passphrase.ts:61-83) has the same residue on every path: neither `bytes` nor `buffer` is ever zeroed, including on backup_passphrase_too_large and Ctrl-C. It also calls `readSync` directly, with no EAGAIN/EINTR retry, unlike `readOnce`. `readStdinValueBytes` (secret-value.ts:172-188) likewise never zeroes its chunk buffers or its `number[]`.

UNVERIFIED (I have no shell)
- That `bun run check` is green (1173 tests), including Biome accepting the new multi-line import block's sort order and format.
- The writer's darwin pty runs for the two new scenarios, and the mutation controls the writer reports (bytes/next zeroing removed; LF not consumed).
- That CI skips the pty cases. By reading, the skip is `process.platform === "darwin"`, so on the Linux ARM64 runner AC2 and AC3 are proven only by local darwin runs.
- How JSC handles array backing stores after pop and growth (the comment NIT).

Follow-up filed for the verdict's out-of-scope LOW (readPassphraseBytes and readStdinValueBytes buffers) and its two small items (assert bytes.length on all four zeroing cases; soften the doc comment to 'the bytes still held'): WCLI-138 (label security), queued behind WCLI-137. Nit E (empty value then CR and a byte) stays open and fails closed. WCLI-136 closes with WCLI-138 as the named residual.
finalSummary: readHiddenValueBytes zeroes its bytes, its one-byte buffer and the byte read after a CR in a finally, so every way out of the hidden reader (a returned value, an abandoned read, the CR multiline refusal and the too_large refusal) clears what it read; only the returned copy survives. Two pty scenarios cover CR terminators (a CR multiline refusal and a CRLF accepting control, LEN:6), and QUIET_MS and POLLIN are shared. Verified: bun run check (1173 pass), lore check, CI Check, Docs and Tracker integrity green at f23c619, mutation controls (each zeroing removed, and the LF no longer consumed, each turn their test red), local darwin pty runs (CI skips pty), and an opus APPROVE at f23c619 (verbatim in the notes). Residual: WCLI-138 (passphrase and stdin buffers, test and comment tightening); nit E left, fails closed.
